Sam —

Thanks — great to meet you and the SpectraPulse team. High level we can offer three reservation pathways that cover the tradeoff between unit economics and activation speed. I attached a short options deck and a cost workbook. Summary below (ballpark monthly committed GPUs shown as equivalent v100-32 slices):

1) Onramp (Conservative start)
- Minimum committed: 8 GPUs
- Typical production cluster: scales to 24 GPUs by week 8 (we provision additional lanes as traffic stabilizes)
- Activation: 2–4 week warm-up; include 100k warm-up token credits and 2-week burst credit to absorb spikes
- Use case: pilot with rapid validation, you pay lower monthly commitment, higher incremental unit price

2) Baseline (Predictable throughput)
- Minimum committed: 32 GPUs
- Ramp: 4 weeks to reach baseline, 8–10 weeks to full 64 GPU footprint if needed
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability, 95th pct tail latency target <200–250ms for 512 tokens on our tuned kernels
- Includes 1 month of activation credits and reduced per-token unit cost vs Onramp

3) Enterprise (Reserved performance)
- Minimum committed: 64 GPUs (can be cross-region; includes reserved bursting lanes)
- Ramp: immediate allocation with two-stage canary (48 GPUs active first 2 weeks, ramp to 64)
- Price: best unit costs, includes placement priority and dedicated support + optional private control plane

Notes on private/VPC: Dedicated can be delivered with VPC peering (hosted dedicated) or as Private (customer-managed control plane) for an additional platform fee. For most customers peering gives the same network isolation while keeping onboarding faster.

Next steps I recommend: review the attached cost workbook, tell us which pathway looks closest to your needs (Onramp/Baseline/Enterprise), and we’ll draft a mutual action plan with exact timelines (we can include a 30–60 day option to add burst capacity). If procurement wants the one-pager we can pull that together by EOW.

I looped Camila (CC) to help with contract terms and activation credits.

Thanks,
